title: Siwa horn
summary: The siwa is a large side-blown horn of the coast of Kenya and Tanzania, carved of wood or ivory and once owned by local chiefs. A hole near the narrow end is blown across, and the wide bell carries a deep, full note.
howToPlay: Four notes of the horn are lit along it, the higher ones nearer the mouth hole.
A band of breath runs from the mouth hole to the note you strike, and rings of sound leave the bell.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It was blown for chiefs on festive occasions along the Swahili coast, a mark of rank as well as a musical instrument.
